_meta.description: Vacuum mode and data-point enums extracted from the Roborock app's Hermes home_card plugin bundle. Names are the app's own identifiers; numeric values are literal constants read from the decompiled bytecode. Only entries the app itself defines are listed - this is not a complete device-side range.
sources: assets/plugin/home_card/robot.vacuum.cleaner/robot.vacuum.cleaner.zip -> index.android.bundle (Hermes bytecode v96, 1156616 bytes, app com.roborock.smart 4.72.02-100920); project.json version 2066, apiLevel 10028

robot.vacuum.cleaner_v2050.zip (Roborock cloud plugin endpoint) -> index.android.bundle.map; project.json version 2050, apiLevel 10028. This source map carries the plugin's ORIGINAL TypeScript/JavaScript sources in sourcesContent - 616 files, project root /Users/weiwei/rockrobo/worksource/cardVacuu.
_meta.method: v2066: hermes-dec (hbc_decompiler.py) -> register-level pseudo JS, constants read from the module initialiser of the listed Metro module id. v2050: original source read straight out of index.android.bundle.map.
_meta.confidence: proven - every value below is a literal constant in the bundle or a literal in the original source
_meta.sourceOfEntry: Entries carry a 'src' field naming the original file (v2050) or a 'moduleId' (v2066 bytecode). Where the two versions differ the entry says so.

105.name: CleanModeZero
105.note: vacuuming off; the app treats fan_power != 105 as 'is vacuuming'

110.name: SmartCleanMode
110.note: SmartPlan; only active when water==209 and mop==306 as well

fanPower.notInBundleNote: 101/103/104 are well established in the community as Quiet/Turbo/Max but are NOT defined in this bundle - do not cite it as evidence for them.

200.name: WaterModeZero
200.note: water off; the app treats water_box_status != 200 as 'is mopping'

modeCombinations.note: The app reports SmartPlan only when all three match, and 'customized' when any of the three matches its custom value.

sweeperDpType.description: Data-point ids the vacuum home_card uses. Keys are the app's names, values the DPS numbers as strings (the app stores them as strings).

dpStatus.note: Typo 'Returing_Dock' is the app's own. This list is the plugin's subset; the native Java layer maps further codes (15,16,17,18,23,28,32,33,34,36,37,38,39,40) - see _appanalysis/05-api-katalog.md section 5.1.

dpCleanTaskType.note: 'Idel' is the app's own spelling. 5 and 6 both map to Part_Clean.

dpBackType.note: 0/3/4 come from the DPBackType enum. 1/2/5 are proven by BackDockStateMap in SweeperStatusManager.ts, which maps back_type 1..5 onto the labels backdock_substate_washing_mop, backdock_substate_setup_mop, backdock_substate_teardown_mop, backdock_substate_collecting_dust and home_new_control_start_charge. The DPBackType enum itself lists 1/2/5 only as source comments.

offlineReason.note: This is the RPC-path encoding, used by the native (get_status) card. Translation keys resolve through roborock_strings.json. Texts: 1 = 'Manual Shutdown', 34 = 'Hibernate Shutdown', 51 = 'Low Battery Shutdown', 103 = 'Upgrading and Restarting'.
offlineReason.supersedes: 11-hermes-plugins.md 2.6 called 2/3/4 'aliases tolerated by the app'. They are not aliases - see offlineReasonOdm.

offlineReasonOdm.description: The SECOND, incompatible encoding of DPS 135. The data-point (ODM) card indexes a four-element array with offlineReasonType - 1, so the device sends 1..4, not 1/34/51/103.
offlineReasonOdm.note: The same app ships both encodings for different device families. roborock.mower uses this same 1..4 form (OFFLINE_STATUS, dpKey 138) - see roborock_other_device_enums.json. Which one applies depends on whether the device speaks the RPC or the data-point protocol.

robotStateCodeMap.description: The state codes the RPC path maps to a display text. This is a DIFFERENT namespace from dpStatus (DPS 121): here 101/102/103 mean offline/unknown/map-saving, whereas on DPS 121 they mean Locating/Cleaning_Only/Mopping_Only. Do not merge the two tables.

15.name: RUB_TO_DOCK
15.note: The app rewrites 15 to 6 and reads exit_dock: exit_dock == 1 shows robot_state_exiting_dock ('Departing from the dock').

26.name: BACK_TO_DOCK_WASHING_DUSTER
26.note: back_type refines this into the backdock_substate_* texts

100.name: FULL_CHARGE
100.note: Synthesised by the app: state == 8 && battery == 100 becomes 100. Not necessarily sent by the device.

getStatusFields.description: The fields the plugin reads out of get_prop(["get_status"]).result[0].
getStatusFields.note: wash_phase is only read by v2066; v2050 does not know it. The live mode values (fan_power / water_box_status / mop_mode) live inside cleaning_info, not at the top level.

inCleaning.description: Resume marker: which kind of task can be continued.
inCleaning.confidence: proven for the running code path
inCleaning.warning: The source contradicts itself: the CleanResumeFlag declaration comments claim 2 = Segment and 3 = Zone, while the CleanResumeFlagCodeMap actually executed maps 2 -> Zone_Clean and 3 -> Segment_Clean. The values above are what the app really does. Verify against a device before relying on 2 vs 3.

washStatus.description: Bit field, evaluated only while state is 23 or 25 (WASHING_DUSTER): low byte = phase state (0 means idle), high byte (>> 8) = mode.
washStatus.note: Only these four modes get a text; every other mode falls back to status_duster_washing. The low byte's own value range is not enumerated anywhere in the plugin.

washPhase.onlyIn: v2066 (the APK bundle) - v2050 does not read this field at all
washPhase.usage: isWorkingOnDock() and hasTask() treat wash_phase == PUMPING as 'not really working / no task'; wash_phase == PUMPING also sets the text wash_towel_phase_pumping.
washPhase.note: Only these two values are named. Answers part of the open wash_phase question from 11-hermes-plugins.md section 10.

commonStatus.description: Bit field on the status object.
commonStatus.confidence: proven for bit 2 and bits 3-4; the rest is commented out in the source

6-9.confidence: commented out in the source - plausible, not active

13.confidence: commented out in the source - plausible, not active

tidyUpStatus.description: Both fields share one layout: low byte = activity (1 = running), bits 8-15 = object type from obstacleNames.
tidyUpStatus.note: Only object types 2, 34 and 51 get a name; anything else falls back to state_doing_tidyup_object / state_doing_move_object.

obstacleNames.description: Map object / obstacle type ids to translation keys. Useful for rendering obstacles on the map.
obstacleNames.note: Translation keys resolve through roborock_strings.json. Known English texts from the card's own bundle: 2 = 'Footwear', 34 = 'Fabric', 51 = 'Fabric/paper balls'.

smartScene.description: Cloud-side 'smart scene' (quick command) objects. Each scene's action item carries a nested RPC call.
smartScene.confidence: proven as the content of a cloud scene object; NOT proven as a call the app itself sends to a device. The string exists only in the source map (a mockSceneList constant and an example comment, both captured from real server responses on a G10 dev account) and is absent from the shipped bytecode of all six bundles. At runtime the app only calls NativeSDK.executeSmartScene(duid, sceneId) and the cloud runs the stored RPC.
smartScene.note: do_scenes_app_start is a method name that appears in NO earlier analysis. source = 101 marks the scene channel, next to the widget's 820 and the device list's 2. mop_template_id and repeat are new parameters. v2066 additionally reads seq_type from the same params object (value range unknown; the string CleanThenMop appears alongside it, so 'vacuum then mop' ordering is plausible but unproven).

newFeatureStrBit.description: Bit indices into the device's newFeatureInfoStr hex string.

decoding.algorithm: nibbleIndex = -floor(bit/4); shift = bit % 4; hexChar = nibbleIndex !== 0 ? newFeatureInfoStr.slice(nibbleIndex-1, nibbleIndex) : newFeatureInfoStr.slice(-1); supported = ((parseInt('0x'+(hexChar||'0')) >> shift) & 1) !== 0
decoding.note: The string is read from the right: bit 0..3 live in the last hex char, bit 4..7 in the one before it, and so on.

deviceControlPaths.description: How the home_card plugin actually issues commands.

viaDataPoints.note: The plugin writes DPBoolean.False (0) for pause/resume/stop, whereas the native home-screen widget writes 1 (see 05-api-katalog.md section 2.1). The original source confirms the 0 is deliberate (DPBoolean.False, not a decoding artefact) and that DPSender passes the value through unchanged into publishDps({ '<dps>': <value> }). Which value the device actually needs is still unresolved - only a capture on real hardware settles it.

viaRpc.note: The plugin sends empty parameter arrays; the native widget sends [{"source":820}] and the device list [{"source":2}].
